notes.meaning: David observes the lifestyle of the wicked and sees the real problem behind their bad choices. Deep down, they have no reverent fear or respect for God. Because they do not honor the Lord as their Judge, they feel free to break His laws without shame.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early writers like Augustine read this verse as the wicked man telling himself in his own heart that he will sin, deliberately refusing to understand God.

notes.meaning: The wicked person deceives himself with flattering thoughts. He convinces himself that his wrongdoing is not that bad and that God will never notice or punish it. He keeps living this lie until his guilt is exposed and everyone sees how hateful his sin really is.

Everything coming out of the wicked man's mouth is dishonest and hurtful. He has turned away from wisdom and refuses to do what is right. Instead of growing in goodness, he has completely walked away from God's path.

Even while resting in bed at night, the wicked person uses the quiet hours to plot evil deeds. When daylight comes, he deliberately commits himself to a destructive way of living. He has hardened his heart so thoroughly that he no longer hates sin at all.

David turns his eyes away from human wickedness to celebrate the limitless goodness of God. The Lord's faithful love is so vast that it reaches to the highest heavens, and His reliability climbs above the clouds. Even when people break their promises, God remains completely faithful forever.

God's righteousness stands firm and unmovable, like the mightiest mountains. His decisions and ways of governing the world are deeper than the ocean, far beyond our ability to fully understand. In His great kindness, the Lord faithfully provides for both human beings and animals.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine saw the high mountains as the apostles who received Christ's light first, while the great deep represented the dark abyss of sin into which the wicked sink.

notes.meaning: David marvels at how precious and costly God's loyal love is to His people. Because God is so kind, people can run to Him and take shelter under the shadow of His wings, like young chicks hiding under a mother bird. Finding our safety in God brings true peace and security.

Those who seek God are richly supplied with the spiritual feast found in His presence. He satisfies their deepest longings and gives them drink from a flowing river of heavenly delights. Believers find a lasting joy in God that the world can never match.

God alone is the fountain of life, the spring from which all physical and spiritual life flows. His divine light shines upon us so that we can clearly see the truth about Him and ourselves. When we walk in fellowship with Him, our darkness is replaced by His wisdom and joy.

David asks God to keep showing His loyal love to those who truly know and honor Him. He prays that the Lord's righteousness will continually protect and defend people whose hearts are sincere. Believers can confidently ask God for the very mercies He has promised to give.

David prays that proud enemies will not be allowed to trample him down or step on him. He asks that the violent hands of wicked men will never drive him from his home or shake his peace. We can turn to God for protection whenever arrogant people try to push us around.

With strong faith, David speaks of the final defeat of evildoers as if it has already taken place. God's enemies are knocked down and will never be able to stand again. In the end, God will completely destroy evil and protect His faithful people forever.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early church writers like Augustine and Jerome understood the word 'there' as referring to pride, viewing pride as the downfall of evil angels and the place where sinners perish.
